title: Finite covers kill classes with constant coefficients (Stacks 09ZD (2))
statement: Let $X$ be an affine scheme [def-pc-scheme], $Z\subseteq X$ a closed subscheme (a closed immersion $Z\to X$ [def-weil-closed-immersion]), $M$ a finite abelian group with constant sheaf $\underline M$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf] on the small etale sites, $q\ge1$ an integer and $\xi\in H^q(Z_{\Et},\underline M)$ a class of etale cohomology [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology]. Then there exists a morphism $X'\to X$ which is finite [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], surjective [def-weil-surjective-morphism] and of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation] such that the pullback [def-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback] of $\xi$ along the projection $X'\times_XZ\to Z$ [def-pc-fibre-product] is zero in $H^q((X'\times_XZ)_{\Et},\underline M)$ (the inverse image of the constant sheaf $\underline M$ on $Z$ being identified with the constant sheaf $\underline M$ on $X'\times_XZ$, [lemma-constructible-pullback-constant]).

proof.text: Apply the integral-cover vanishing theorem to X to obtain an integral surjective π:T→X. The base change pullback.fst π i of the closed immersion is closed, so the constant sheaf on T×_X Z has zero positive derived cohomology.

proof.text: Convert this zero object to a subsingleton Sheaf.H group. Functor.homologyRightDerivedFunctorObjSingleFunctorIso identifies total derived global sections on a single sheaf with classical right-derived Γ. Sheaf.ΓNatIsoSheafSections identifies Γ with terminal evaluation; applying NatTrans.rightDerived to its hom and inverse gives an isomorphism of derived functors. The positive-degree Ext/evaluation comparison then gives the subsingleton. Injectivity of H applied to upperStarConstantSheafIso shows that the unadjusted cohomologyMap of ξ on T×_X Z is zero.

proof.text: Use Scheme.Hom.exists_finiteApproximation_of_isIntegralHom to present π as a cofiltered limit F of finite finitely presented X-schemes. Lift its cone to Over X using Over.liftCone and Over.isLimitLiftCone, then map it by Over.pullback i followed by Over.forget Z. The pullback functor is a right adjoint and hence preserves limits; the forgetful functor preserves connected limits, and a cofiltered category is nonempty and connected. Thus the mapped cone is a limit with point T×_X Z and stages F_j×_X Z. These stages are affine, since F_j and Z are affine over X; hence they are qcqs and their transition morphisms are affine.

proof.text: Apply exists_cofiltered_etale_cohomology_cocone to this diagram and the constant sheaf on Z. Its compatibility equations identify the image of every stage restriction of ξ in its colimit with the limit restriction. The latter is zero by step 2, because pullback.lift_snd identifies the composite of each limit projection and stage projection to Z with pullback.snd π i.

proof.text: By injectivity of the cocone comparison isomorphism, the stage restriction and zero have the same image in the colimit. The forgetful functor from AddCommGrpCat in universe u+1 preserves filtered colimits indexed in universe u. Mathlib Limits.IsColimit.eq_iff' therefore supplies an arrow to a stage where the images agree. The cocone theorem's compatibility equation H(f.op)(r_k ξ)=r_j ξ identifies this image with that stage's restriction of ξ, so it is zero.

proof.text: Choose that finite stage F_j→X. It is finite and finitely presented by the approximation. It is surjective because F.π.app j ≫ F.p j = π is surjective, by Surjective.of_comp. Its restriction of ξ is zero by step 5; applying the constant-sheaf coefficient comparison sends zero to zero, giving exactly the target conclusion.
